newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana Airways seeks two new planes.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Airways seeks two new planes.

text.p: Ghana Airways is seeking two planes to replace the DC-9 airliner that ensured its service along the coast of West Africa until it crash-landed at Ivory Coast's Abidjan airport on April 12, its chief executive said.
"We have been told that the cost of repairing it is higher than the insurance compensation we will get for it," Rex Lezard told Joy-FM radio in Accra.
"We are considering acquiring two new airplanes. There are two ways of acquiring -- purchasing and leasing," he said, adding that the company planned to use insurance money to acquire the new planes.
Lezard, interviewed on Friday, said that it would take two to four weeks before the planes became operational.
The west coast service was a major source of revenue with an average passenger load factor of 59 percent in 1996.

The DC-9 was 19 years old and wholly owned by Ghana Airways. The airline wholly owns one other plane, a 15-year-old DC-10, and leases a 23-year- old DC-10 from Belgian Skyjet. Both planes fly on South and East Africa and intercontinental routes.
Lezard is from wholly owned British Airways Speedwing Consulting Ltd, which won a two-year management contract in July 1995 to prepare Ghana Airways for privatisation.
